messages:
laura: Quick question — we need a cross-SDK policy for error semantics & where retries live. transports differ (fetch / requests / grpc). I sketched a minimal idea: normalize to an SDKError with keys {code, retriable, rawStatus, metadata}. Example:```ts
// TS surface
throw new SDKError({ code: 'ERR_TIMEOUT', retriable: true, rawStatus: 504, meta: {requestId} })
```
Should transports swallow/http-wrap or should SDK layer translate? Also how do we treat pagination/resume tokens vs transport-level failures?
sam: +1 on normalizing. My take: transport should only handle transport-level retries (tcp, transient DNS, basic idempotent retries). SDK should be responsible for application-level retries and backoff decisions (e.g., when to retry a generate call vs not). That way language transports can optimize but semantics stay same.
ajay: Tradeoff: if transport does automatic retries you lose visibility into original failures unless we attach rawStatus. We should preserve a chain: SDKError.cause -> rawTransportError. Also we need an "idempotency_hint" on calls used by SDK for safe retries (esp pagination, streaming).
maria: For streaming & long-polling: we need to differentiate ephemeral errors (reconnectable) vs terminal errors (bad auth, invalid payload). Proposal: add field "terminal" boolean and surface an enum reason: AUTH, PAYLOAD, RATE_LIMIT, TRANSIENT. Streaming clients can decide whether to resume.
ben: agree w/ Ajay re: preserving metadata. Please avoid swallowing trace headers. attach all transport headers into SDKError.meta.raw_headers. Observability depends on that.
laura: What about language ergonomics? Python: exceptions, TS: throw, Go: (err, nil). We still want a canonical code set. Maybe use stable error codes strings (+HTTP/gRPC codes in meta).
sam: Suggest canonical codes: ERR_TIMEOUT, ERR_TRANSIENT, ERR_RATE_LIMIT, ERR_AUTH, ERR_PAYLOAD, ERR_QUOTA. SDKs map transport-specific codes to these. Add boolean retriable and an optional retry_after for rate limits.
ajay: Quick mapping sketch:```text
HTTP 408/504 -> ERR_TIMEOUT, retriable=true
HTTP 429 -> ERR_RATE_LIMIT, retriable=true, retry_after=Retry-After
HTTP 401 -> ERR_AUTH, retriable=false
gRPC UNAVAILABLE -> ERR_TRANSIENT, retriable=true
gRPC PERMISSION_DENIED -> ERR_AUTH, retriable=false
```
maria: For pagination/resume token flows: if a token becomes invalid (400 w/ reason=invalid_cursor) treat as terminal and surface a PaginationInvalid error with `can_resume=false`. For transient network blips between pages, SDK should transparently retry page fetches up to x times before surfacing.
ben: Implementation note: keep transport as a thin pluggable layer that returns (ok | transportError) plus raw metadata. SDK layer composes into SDKError. This keeps transports simple to optimize per-language.
laura: Tests + compatibility: we should add a cross-language golden set of error cases (HTTP, grpc, streaming disconnects, malformed resume token) and assert canonical codes + presence of raw meta. Who wants to draft the RFC PR?
sam: happy to pair on the PR for the mapping table.
ajay: I can add test vectors to the harness (will need sample server to emit codes and headers).
maria: I'll prototype streaming classification logic this week and share results.
ben: I'll start the TS/Go mapping module PR and include examples for how raw headers are attached:```ts
class SDKError extends Error {
  code: string;
  retriable: boolean;
  rawStatus?: number;
  meta?: Record<string, any>; // includes raw_headers, transport, cause
}
```
laura: Awesome — thanks all. Let's sync in #eng-platform tomorrow 11am to finalize the canonical codes and feature-flag plan for toggling SDK retries vs transport.
